title: Arguments and default values
subtitle: Pass values by position or parameter name. Give a parameter a default for common cases.
concept: Pass values by position or parameter name. Give a parameter a default for common cases.
intuition: Order drinks by specifying price and quantity. If no quantity is given, prepare one.
objectives: Give a common value a default
Decide whether a list input may change

body.title: Identify what each input means
body.text: def cost(price, count): has two parameters. cost(3, 2) passes 3 to price and 2 to count by position, producing 6. Reordering arguments can change their meaning. State the units of inputs such as unit price and quantity.

body.title: Give a common value a default
body.text: def cost(price, count=1): uses 1 when count is omitted. cost(3) buys one item; cost(3, 2) buys two. cost(price=3, count=2) uses keyword arguments to name the parameters explicitly. Here the defaulted parameter follows the required one.

body.title: Decide whether a list input may change
body.text: To total a list, read its items and return total without adding to or deleting from the input. This makes the function easier to predict. Start with numbers or strings as defaults: a default [] can be shared across calls. The optional note explains why.

formalDefinition.text: Arguments can be supplied by position or by name. A default applies when its argument is omitted.
conditions: An explicit argument overrides the default. Required parameters precede defaulted parameters here.

interactiveVisual.prediction: With unit price 3 and quantity 2, what is returned?

workedExamples.title: One item by default
workedExamples.problem: At unit price 3, buy one item and then two.

answer.code:
def cost(price, count=1):
    return price * count

print(cost(3))
print(cost(3, 2))

commonMistakes.claim: Passing quantity 0 still activates the default 1.
commonMistakes.correction: An explicit 0 is used as 0. The default applies only when the argument is omitted.

commonMistakes.claim: Positional arguments can be reordered freely.
commonMistakes.correction: Each position corresponds to a parameter. Use keyword arguments when the order is unclear.

practice.problem: Use unit price 5 and the default quantity 1.
Call with unit price 5 and quantity 2 using parameter names.
Write total_of to read [2, 3] and return its sum.
practice.hint: Do not modify the input list.
solution: The original list still has two items.

answer.code:
def total_of(values):
    total = 0
    for value in values:
        total = total + value
    return total

values = [2, 3]
print(total_of(values))
print(values)

practice.problem: What is the cost of quantity 0 at unit price 5?

learningCheck.question: For cost(price, count=1), what is count in cost(5, 0)?
choices: 5, because argument order does not matter
learningCheck.explanation: An explicit argument overrides its default.
feedback: A default is used only when that argument is omitted.
Yes. Passing 0 computes the price of zero items.
The second position supplies count, not the first.

furtherReading.title: Optional: why [] is a risky default
furtherReading.text: A default value is created once when the function is defined. In def add(item, items=[]):, appending to items makes calls that omit items share one list. Use items=None, then if items is None: items = [] inside the function. None marks an omitted list, and is None checks for that marker. Beginners can instead make the list argument required to avoid hidden state.
